overview: This table sets the rules for each wave of a Story, Arcade, or computer-opponent mission, including the battlefield, enemies, time, goals, and music.
description: Shared per-wave configuration for Story, Arcade and PvE battles: spawn layout, time/force-gauge rules, enemy slots and revival flags, order/task links and battle music.

Id.simple: The name that identifies this wave and connects it to missions, results, and previews.
Id.technical: FName import key/row name for FGameDataTableRow_MissionWave (the export spells the column `ID`). Waves are looked up by ids from Arcade missions and StoryMissionWave rows, or by ids picked from PvEMissionWaveLottery rows. The PvE picker initializes its output with `PVE_X_WAVE_0000`, which is itself an exported row, so an empty/failed lottery can leave a fallback wave rather than a null. On PvE result entry the wave's Id is appended to PvESettings.PickedWaveIds; that list is later used to halve the weight of previously used waves. The id is also passed as the PvE situation-overview wave id.

MissionLayoutIndex.simple: Chooses which prepared battlefield layout provides the fighters' starting positions on stages that support it.
MissionLayoutIndex.technical: int32, default 0. It indexes the current Map row's `Id_MissionLayout` array (16 entries in the export), not MissionLayoutDataTables directly. GetCharacterStartTransform applies a layout only when the map row is found, `IsValidIndex(MissionLayoutIndex)` is true and that slot is not None; the id then resolves through MissionLayoutDataTables, overriding translation/rotation components that are valid for the character slot. -1, an out-of-range index or a None slot keeps the battle-area transform. Exported values are -1 (133 rows) and 0-13.

TimeLimit.simple: Controls the wave's time limit, with larger values giving more time. Negative means unlimited time and zero uses the mission or level default.
TimeLimit.technical: float, default 0.0f, in seconds. In mission phases, a value > 0 wins over StudioBattleLevelRequest_CA0.TimeLimit and Global TimeLimit[0]; a value < 0 makes GetBattleTimeLimitInfinite return true regardless of the level request's bTimeLimitInfinity; 0 falls back to the level/global setting. The versus-enemy interval widget shows a special infinite label for negative values and, for 0, uses Global TimeLimit[0] only when that array is nonempty. Exported rows use -1, 0 and positive values from 30 to 360.

ForceGaugeMax.simple: Sets the opposing team's shared gauge for the wave. Larger values allow more knockouts, and negative values make the gauge unlimited.
ForceGaugeMax.technical: int32, default 0. Mission and PvE GetBattleSideRule read it for Side==1: 0 becomes the default 4, while any other value is returned unchanged. ApplyBattleRules feeds that result to SetCharacterStockMax/SetCharacterStock and calls SetCharacterStockUnlimited when it is negative, so the exported -1 (113 rows) means unlimited stock. Mission-base Side 0 stays 4; PvE Side 0 is instead computed from binding vows. Exports also use 1-4.

Id_MissionCharacter_Enemy.simple: Names the computer-controlled fighters in this wave, in the order the game adds them. An empty name leaves that place unused.
Id_MissionCharacter_Enemy.technical: TArray<FName>, default empty. Exported rows have four slots padded with None. Story entry setup iterates all slots, skipping None/missing MissionCharacter rows; Arcade and PvE entry builders use slot `Index-2` for battle slots 2+ without bounds or None checks. Several UI previews first resolve the mission's wave 0 and then read this array; IntervalArcade_BattlePairFromWave uses the leading non-None count, while Story_GetBattleLayout uses the total non-None count together with the ally count. Preload paths gather unique character ids from all non-None entries.

bRevivalEnabled.simple: Chooses whether each enemy can recover after being knocked down. On lets them get back up and keep fighting.
bRevivalEnabled.technical: TArray<bool>, default empty; every exported row has four entries. It is aligned with the enemy slots and copied by index into FStudioBattleCharacterSetup::StatusSetup.Byte4D (Story `Index`; Arcade/PvE `Index-2`). Byte4D==1 permits a BounceUp follow-up only when the extra movement/defeated/armor conditions also hold, prevents DownEnd disappearance/deactivation of a defeated character when ActionControllerSlot181(0) is false, and blocks down-recovery completion before Global Dead_Time. Byte4D!=1 allows that disappearance, and CP_150 releases traps on deactivation. Both true and false entries occur in the export.

Id_MissionOrder.simple: Names the wave's mission goal, such as a boss fight. It also sets the objective text shown during the fight.
Id_MissionOrder.technical: FName, default None. Resolved against MissionOrderDataTables (DTM+0x9D0) in SetupArcade/SetupPvE/SetupStory and in many widgets; Battle_FindMissionOrderRow with bCheckNone=true returns null for None. The order row controls win/result checks, name/detail text, boss versus normal transition variants and boss cost/radar checks, and IntervalPvE uses its ExcludeBindingVowsEffectType to filter vow candidates. The order id, not the wave row id, is what is passed to PlayBattleStartMissionWave/SetMissionWaveInfo.

Id_MissionTaskLottery.simple: Names the group of tasks the game randomly picks from for this wave. The chosen task appears in the battle task display.
Id_MissionTaskLottery.technical: FName, default None. Story and Arcade setup and GamePvE_MakeMissionTasks call BattleArcade_PickLotteryTask on it: a null row or empty task/weight arrays yields NAME_None; otherwise None tasks are removed with their weights and one task is picked randomly in proportion to the remaining weights. Story_GetDemoMissionTask instead takes the first candidate from the lottery row. Exported rows contain None and 134 named lotteries.

Id_Bgm.simple: Names the battle music played for this wave. If none is set, the game uses the mission's music or standard battle music.
Id_Bgm.technical: FName, default None. Mission-base GetBattleBgmName resolves it through BgmDataTables with bCheckNone=true; if no row is found it retries StudioBattleLevelRequest_CA0.BgmId and finally returns BGM_BATTLE_01. With no current wave it proceeds directly to the level-request path. A found row contributes its CueSheetName string as an FName (empty name when that string is empty). Exported rows contain 11 named BGM ids and None.

notes: The only exported MissionWaveDataTable variant has 1,774 unique row keys; every row has nine fields, its key equals its `ID`, and both parallel arrays have four entries. The manager registers the table as MissionWaveDataTables (DTM+0x9A0). StoryMissionWaveDataTable is a separate story-wave-to-MissionWave join table.

The active wave is cached in FStudioBattleMissionTaskSystem: SetupArcade/SetupPvE/SetupStory store the resolved row array and select MissionWave = MissionWaves[RetryCount], exposed by GetMissionWave/GetMissionWaves. Most phase/UI consumers use that cache; interval and menu paths resolve rows directly from ids.

Cross-export check: every non-None enemy id, task lottery, mission order and BGM id referenced by the 1,774 rows resolves in the corresponding available export, as do all 90 distinct ArcadeMission wave ids and 1,589 distinct PvEMissionWaveLottery wave ids. One StoryMissionWave row (`STMSN_06090S`) references a MissionWave id that is absent from the export.

Exported arrays are fixed-width and None-padded; consumers do not consistently validate parallel lengths. Story indexes bRevivalEnabled[Index] after checking the enemy id, while Arcade/PvE use `Index-2` without bounds checks.

Finders and entry builders are reconstructed (status/functions.json labels several of these functions behavioural). Claims describe reconstructed native behavior; no complete retail Blueprint call graph was available because Content is partial.

usages.detail: Uses MissionLayoutIndex against the current map row's Id_MissionLayout and applies the resolved layout transform.
Uses TimeLimit, ForceGaugeMax and Id_Bgm for the time limit, infinite flag, side-1 stock and BGM fallback.
Applies the derived side rule as character stock max/stock and marks negative rules unlimited.
Resolves story mission waves into MissionWave rows and builds enemy entries from Id_MissionCharacter_Enemy and bRevivalEnabled.
Arcade setup resolves every wave and picks a task from Id_MissionTaskLottery.
Caches the wave array, current wave, mission order and task for the active retry index.
Derives BattlePair from the leading non-None enemy slots; the first wave also drives previews and character preloading.
Picks PvE wave ids (including the PVE_X_WAVE_0000 sentinel) and rolls task ids from Id_MissionTaskLottery.
Story launch layout uses the MissionWave's non-None enemy count together with the Story wave's ally count.
First-wave enemy list drives root-select previews and character texture gathering.
